hunts.label: Wednesday, Nov 11
hunts.subtitle: A frosty, windless morning, when every leaf tells tales. Sit first, walk later.

rules.title: Same-morning plan
items: This plan was built at 6:08 am. Legal light is 6:10, so you walk in at legal light, not 45 minutes before it.
Walk slow and quiet. With no wind and cold air, sound carries far. Load only when you reach the seat.
Wednesday is a **crow day** (Wed, Fri, Sat only).
No clock change before this hunt.
rules.note: Small game focus today, by your request. Deer is open, but this load has no buckshot.

conditions.source: Hourly forecast service (the National Weather Service point forecast was stale this morning)
items: Walk-in: about **40F**, frost likely on open ground. 9 am: about **55F**.
Wind: **calm**, 0 to 2 mph, drifting N to NE then E.
Sky: **clear**, 0 to 1 percent cloud. Rain chance 1 to 2 percent.
Humidity: 92 percent at 7 am, 71 percent by 9 am. Expect dew and frost melt.
Moon: **waxing crescent, about 5 percent**. Moonrise 9:06 am, so the night was dark.
conditions.meaning: Assumption: a dark, cold, clear, calm night after a new moon means animals fed early in the night and will move again in daylight. Squirrels will wait for the sun and get busy from about 7:15 to 9:00 on sunlit trunks.
conditions.hours_note: The hourly source began at 7 am. The 4 to 6 am hours were not available. Expect about 38 to 40F before 7 am (assumption).

in_season.tip: Sunny edges of thick cover after a frost.
Last ones heading to dens at first light.
Calm, clear mornings bring an early, high fly-out.
Opportunity only. Shoot north, never toward the field SE.
Opportunity at the swamp mud. HIP and plug required.
Skip unless you carry steel shot, HIP, federal stamp, and the state waterfowl privilege.
Open, but not today: no buckshot in this load.

in_season: Bear and bobcat are open. You do not hunt them. Stay aware near the swamp.

plan.title: Sun-at-Back Seat
plan.why: Calm, frosty air means you cannot hide by wind, and frost makes every step loud. So sit first and walk later. On a clear morning the sun lights the **east sides** of the trunks first, and squirrels climb into that warmth. Sit on the east part of the loop interior and face **NW**. The sun is behind you: the squirrels see glare, and you see lit fur on lit trunks. In calm air your scent drifts slowly downhill to the north. That is a small cost for squirrels and it keeps you clear of the house SW and field SE.

steps.text: Leave the yard by the main trail. Red light only. Walk 20 steps, stop 10 seconds, repeat.
Turn off onto the loop trail. At the east leg, step 20 to 30 yards west into the interior. Pick a wide pine or holly with the rising sun behind it. Face NW. Load #4. Plug in.
Sunrise. Do not move. Watch the lit faces of trunks 20 to 40 yards out, from W-NW round to N-NE. Listen for cuttings falling and claws on bark.
Peak squirrel time starts as the sun warms the trunks. Try the leaf-scratch call (see the squirrel card) once every 10 minutes.
Frost is melting and the leaves go quiet. Still-hunt north to the swamp edge. 3 steps, 20 seconds still. Crow check: listen for fly-out calls.
Turn west along the swamp toward the Junction. Watch the swamp-side pines in full sun. Shots N only toward the swamp, with the ground as backstop.
Loop south to the feed bins. Check the sunny side of thick cover for rabbits. Shoot N or W only from here; never toward the field or the south line.
Unload at the bins. Walk out by the main trail. Do the land task on the way.

items: **In the gun: #4** (plug in, 3 shells max). Good for squirrel to 35 yards.
**Right pocket: #7.5** for crow, dove, snipe, or a close rabbit.
**Slugs: zipped in a separate pocket.** Bear defense only.
**No 00 buckshot today.** It stays home with the deer plan.
**.22 LR (optional):** head shots on still squirrels only, with a trunk or the ground behind the squirrel. Never at a squirrel against the sky.
warnings: Never shoot a deer with birdshot. Not with #4, not with #7.5.
Swap shells in the open with the muzzle north. Count every shell in and out.
Frosty logs are slick. Unload before you cross a log or the swamp edge.

animals.name: Gray squirrel
paragraphs: The most common game on the property. They feed under the pines and in the few hardwoods, and they nest in leaf nests high in the trees.
On a cold, clear, calm morning they stay in the nest until the sun hits. Expect little before 7:00, then a busy hour as the trunks warm. In calm air they hear you from far away, so sit still.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #4 at 20 to 35 yards. Aim at the head and front shoulders.
With the .22: head only, with wood or ground behind it.
After the shot, wait 10 minutes. Others freeze and then move again.
details.note: Mark the fall against a trunk or a stump before you move.

details.title: Call: leaf scratch
steps: Reach down and rake dry leaves with your fingers.
Make 3 or 4 short scratches, pause 2 seconds, then 3 or 4 more.
Stop for 10 minutes. Watch for a head or a tail flick.
It sounds like a squirrel digging for a nut. It brings out the curious ones.
details.note: Use it only from the seat. Keep your hands low and slow.

after: Tip: in full sun, look for the bright edge of the tail first, not the body.
Tip: a squirrel that circles the trunk away from you will come back around if you stay still for 2 minutes.

animals.name: Rabbit
paragraphs: Cottontails use the thick edges near the feed bins and the pine-holly thickets.
After a frost they sit in the first sunny spot at the edge of cover to warm up. They sit very still and trust their color.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #4 or #7.5 at 15 to 25 yards. Aim at the head and front shoulders.
Shoot only when the rabbit is on the ground with the ground behind it.
Never shoot a running rabbit toward the south line or the field.

details.title: Technique: frost-melt spots
steps: Walk the sunny edge of a thicket slowly.
Look for a small dark spot where the frost has melted. A rabbit sat there.
Look for the round black eye and the ear line, not the whole body.
Stop 15 yards short. Wait 30 seconds. A rabbit that thinks it is seen will run.

after: Tip: wear gloves to clean rabbits. Check the liver for white spots and discard the rabbit if you find them.

animals.name: Raccoon and opossum
paragraphs: Both feed at night along the swamp and around the feed bins. At first light the last ones head to dens in hollow trees and under roots.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #4 to the head at 20 yards or less.
Approach from behind. Touch the eye with a stick to confirm it is dead. Opossums play dead.
details.note: Wear gloves. Rabies is possible in raccoons.

after: Tip: a fresh muddy track on the frost near the bins means one passed in the last few hours.

animals.name: Crow
paragraphs: Crows roost outside the property and fly over to feed. On a calm, clear morning they leave the roost early and fly high, then drop lower as they find food.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #7.5 at 35 yards or less. Swing through the bird and keep the gun moving.
Shoot north only, with no house or field beyond the bird.

details.title: Technique: shadow seat
steps: Sit in shade, not sun. Crows see a shiny face at 100 yards.
Keep your face down and look up with your eyes, not your head.
Shoot the first bird that sets its wings and drops.

after: Tip: if one crow falls, wait. The flock often circles back once.

animals.name: Bear and bobcat
paragraphs: Awareness only. Both are in the area. Give a bear space, talk out loud, and back away. Slugs are for defense only.

skill.title: Still-hunting on a frosty, calm morning
skill.principle: You can hide from eyes by not moving, and from ears by moving with the woods. On a calm, frosty morning the woods make no noise, so you must wait for the frost to melt or move so slowly that you sound like an animal, not a person.

sections.title: Before you move
steps: Check the frost. Press a leaf with your boot. If it crunches, stay seated.
Look at the full lane ahead. Pick your next stop, 3 steps away, beside a tree.
Plan where each foot goes: bare dirt, moss, pine needles, or a root.

sections.title: The step
steps: Lift your foot high, so you do not drag it through leaves.
Put the outside edge of your foot down first, then roll to the flat of the foot.
Shift your weight only when the foot is quiet.
Take 3 steps. Then stand still for 20 seconds.
In those 20 seconds, look near, then middle, then far. Look for parts, not whole animals.

sections.title: When you hear something
steps: Freeze in mid-step if you must.
Move only your eyes for 30 seconds.
Raise the gun only when the animal's head is behind a trunk.

details.title: Why the rhythm matters
paragraphs: People walk at a steady beat. Animals move, stop, and move again. A steady crunch-crunch-crunch is a person. Three steps and a long stop sounds like a squirrel or a deer feeding.

skill.checkpoint: Before 8:15, still-hunt 50 yards and count your steps. Write down how many minutes it took and whether any animal moved before it saw you. Send it with note:.

land.intro: Frost is the best tracking snow you will get this fall. Fresh tracks show dark on white until about 8 am.
steps: On the walk out, count every set of tracks that crosses the main trail between the Junction and the yard.
For each one: pace it from the Junction, and note the direction (toward the swamp or away).
Note any track that is dark and clear (made after the frost) versus dull and frosted over (made before).
Send what you find with a note: message, for example: note: frost tracks, 3 crossings, 40 paces from Junction, toward swamp.

safety: NEVER shoot south. The house is SW and the field is SE: no-shoot directions.
Every shot today goes between W-NW and N-NE, with the ground or a trunk behind the animal.
Hunter orange hat and vest are required (Oct 17 to Jan 1).
Frost and dew make logs, roots, and swamp edges slick. Unload before you cross them.
It is about 40F at walk-in. Wear layers you can open as it warms to 55F by 9 am.
No shots at birds against open sky toward the south line.
hunts.regs: Check seasons, bag limits, and rules in the current NCWRC Regulations Digest before you hunt.
hunts.gaps: The National Weather Service point forecast was stale (Oct 24 data), so another hourly source was used; 4 to 6 am hourly values were not available. Moon illumination was listed as both 5 and 8 percent; 5 percent is used. Migratory bird dates (dove, ducks, snipe, rails) come from last week's check; they were not checked again this morning. Legal light is sunrise minus 30 minutes.
